description:
## Reproduction

```
fn main(), do: dbg(Enum.sort(1..3))
```

```
thread 'main' panicked at src/compiler2/jobs/transport.rs:1448:9:
a resume payload value must have an analyzed type: ValueId(4) in executable
ExecutableKey { activation: ActivationKey { root: RootId(0), function: FunctionId(0), arrow: Ty(33) }, need: Value }
```

Identical on `interp` and `run`, so it is upstream of the doors -- the program never finishes compiling. This is a compiler panic with a backtrace, not a diagnostic: no span, no source location, nothing naming `Enum.sort` or the range.

## Not the whole `Enumerable` half

Other `Enumerable.t(a)`-typed functions take a range without complaint:

```
Enum.filter(1..10, fn x -> x > 5 end)   #=> [6, 7, 8, 9, 10]
Enum.take(1..10, 3)                     #=> [1, 2, 3]
```

So the fault is specific to the `sort` family rather than to ranges reaching `Enum`, which narrows it considerably.

## Why P1

Every other bug this epic has turned up was a wrong answer or a refusal. This one is an unhandled panic on a program a user would reasonably write, and `Enum.sort/1` over a range is not an exotic call. The assertion at `transport.rs:1448` is a real invariant -- a resume payload without an analyzed type -- so something upstream is publishing a resume edge whose value never got a type, and finding that is the fix. A loud panic is the right failure over a silent miscompile, but a diagnostic naming the call would be better than a backtrace either way.

## Found how

Verifying doc examples for `Enum.sort/1`. The example was written against a range first, which crashed; the doc that shipped uses a list instead, so the library's own documentation does not exercise this path.

comments.text: Root cause: Enum.sort/2 sent its Enumerable directly into list-only merge-sort helpers. A Range therefore reached split_sort_list/3, which had no matching clause and settled as a non-returning call. Activation analysis correctly kept that return absent while the fixpoint climbed, but executable projection failed to close settled absence into the empty type, so a structurally retained DeliveredResume reached transport without a payload type. The fix materializes Enum.sort/2 through to_list/1 and records settled non-returning direct and closure call results as none at the semantic-to-executable boundary. Regressions cover Range sort/1 and sort/2 on interp/JIT/AOT plus direct and closure non-returning non-tail calls preserving function_clause. Docs now describe the settled-bottom rule and the Enum example exercises a Range. Gates: cargo fmt check; cargo clippy workspace/all-targets with warnings denied; workspace lib tests 1982 + runtime 225; fixture matrix 648; fz2_cli 30; aot_variadic_open 1; doctests green. Commit 8e17e016f.

title: [BUG] Enum.sort/1 on a Range panics the compiler: a resume payload value must have an analyzed type
